Read-level data can extracted modBam files (standard bam file modification data stored MM ML tags, see SAMtags.pdf) using readModBam(). preferred way described . Alternatively, read-level modification data can also extracted modBam files using modkit (see modkitExtract() calling modkit R readModkitExtract() read resulting output file). require local installation modkit may interest specific modkit features used available otherwise. footprintR package contains small example modBam files generated using Dorado aligner: Modification data read files using readModBam(): create RangedSummarizedExperiment object positions rows: Just like summary-level data, columns correspond samples sample names sample column obtained input files (extractfiles), files named automatically assigned (using "s1", "s2" , assuming file corresponds separate sample). title: Exploring read-level footprinting data with `footprintR`
text: Amongst things, single-molecule footprinting data allows measure average distance neighboring nucleosome particles, called nucleosome repeat length NRL. Traditionally, measured using MNase-seq data (phasogram analysis, see Valouev et al., Nature 2011, doi:10.1038/nature10002), required millions reads accurate estimate. switching measuring distances modified bases within reads, can extract much information per read already manage get accurate estimates handful reads:
code: moddist <- calcModbaseSpacing(se) print(estimateNRL(moddist$sample1)[1:2]) #> $nrl #> [1] 182.6 #>  #> $nrl.CI95 #>    2.5 %   97.5 %  #> 179.5475 185.6525 plotModbaseSpacing(moddist$sample1) plotModbaseSpacing(moddist$sample1, detailedPlots = TRUE)

title: Summarize a read-level object to sample-level. — addReadsSummary
text: se SummarizedExperiment object read-level footprinting data. Rows correspond positions columns samples. assay.type character scalar specifying assay se containing read-level data summarized. Typically, assay contains modification probabilities. statistics Character vector specifying type statistics computed. Currently supported values "Nmod" (number modification probabilities greater equal 0.5), "Nvalid" (number overlapping reads), "FracMod" (Nmod/Nvalid fraction), "Pmod" (average modification probability), "AvgConf" (average confidence (non-)modification probabilities). keep.reads logical scalar. TRUE (default), read-level data assay.type retained assay name. replace.existing logical scalar. TRUE (default), existing assays name ones requested overwritten. Otherwise, existing assays retained corresponding summary statistic(s) recalculated. verbose TRUE, report progress.
